newsitem.title: UK: P&O shares hit by partner's profit slide.
newsitem.headline: P&O shares hit by partner's profit slide.

text.p: Shares in Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co tumbled on Thursday after its Dutch container shipping partner Konkinlijke Nedlloyd Groep NV announced a 54 percent slide in net profit.
Nedlloyd, which merged its container shipping operations with those of P&O last year, said it was too early to make a forecast for the P&O Nedlloyd joint venture.

The Dutch group added that it expected continuing pressure on rates in the current year and the merger's advantages will become more visible in the course of the year, but were not yet visible in the first quarter.

"Nedlloyd is not giving a forecast, which they normally do," commented Peter Bergius, industry analyst at ABN Amro Hoare Govett. "They are saying quarter one is weak for containers and volumes are weak, they fear there will be a further downturn in pricing too, so the deal with P&O looks to be more of a necessity to enable them to compete."
Bergius said he maintains his "sell" rating on P&O shares.

"Twelve months ago this partnership was being heralded as a major turnaround in the companies fortunes, but now the market perceives that the underlying trading position is deteriorating so the total benefits will not be coming through."
